subject: Animation
title: Pete Docter: Pixar's Emotional Core
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Pete Docter: Pixar's Emotional Core.

hook.text: Pete Docter directed Monsters, Inc., Up, Inside Out, and Soul — four of Pixar's most emotionally ambitious films.

buildup.text: Docter specializes in finding emotional truth in impossible concepts — a monster's closet, emotions as characters.

discovery.text: The opening montage of Up made audiences cry in four minutes. It is considered a masterclass in visual storytelling.

twist.text: Docter was 11 years old when he made his first animated film and joined Pixar as its third animator ever.

climax.text: Docter became Pixar's chief creative officer, guiding the studio's emotional and artistic direction.

punchline.text: A kid who made cartoons at eleven now runs Pixar.

quiz.question: What makes Pete Docter's directing style distinctive at Pixar?
options: He focuses exclusively on action-adventure stories
He finds emotional truth in impossible concepts, creating deeply moving films from abstract ideas
